"chwarter wedi naw" is 09:15 and "hanner awr wedi tri" is 03:30 -- the
English direction, NOT the Icelandic one that names the coming hour.

mutation on it: "chwarter i bedwar" is 03:45, "chwarter i dri" 02:45.

blwyddyn (feminine), plural blynyddoedd, with the DEDICATED count
form blynedd used directly after a numeral.  That count form is the
richest mutation case in the language's temporal vocabulary: it
surfaces three ways depending on which numeral precedes it --
blynedd   radical, after three ("tair blynedd")
flynedd   soft b -> f, after two ("dwy flynedd")
mlynedd   nasal b -> m, after five ("pum mlynedd")
all three attested: the first in running text on cy.wikipedia.org,
the latter two on the en.wiktionary.org entry itself.

The wide name is the head noun "dydd" (day) plus the day's own name.
"dydd" is the target of soft mutation after the markers that open an
adverbial "on <weekday>" ("ar ddydd Llun", "bob ddydd Sul"), so the
mutated head is listed beside the radical; attested in running text on
cy.wikipedia.org ("ar ddydd Llun", "o ddydd Llun i ddydd Sadwrn").
Soft-mutated surfaces are listed beside the radical: Welsh changes a
word's first letter after a preceding trigger, so a matcher that saw
only the radical would miss the form running text actually carries.
